items.title: Rick Margitza interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 22, 2024
items.q: maybe a little intimidated by the older generation like am I ready to play with these guys, am I good enough.

ctx.x: I’m looking — here’s where we’re going. I’ll sort of wrap up with — on both sides of me in my office here I have a list of sort of a discography of you. And it has all your solo, your records under your own name and so I’m going to pick two things that you did and
see if you have a memory or comment about them. And I’ll start with Ellis Marsalis, “A Night at Snug Harbor.” What do you remember about that date?

Well Snug Harbor is one of the only clubs — few clubs at that time that was doing modern jazz, so that’s where I played almost all the time. Other than that I was doing weddings and club dates and stuff like that. I remember it being a little chaotic because there was a cast of characters and not everybody played on every song so there was a lot of kind of moving around. There wasn’t that much planned in advance other than a possibility of a couple of different songs, so a little bit chaotic. But knowing…
